title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Juvenile Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of the Juvenile Courts

Fa Fa [2010] No. 32

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of the Juvenile Courts, as issued by the Supreme People's Court, are hereby transmitted to you for diligent implementation.

July 23, 2010

Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of the Juvenile Courts

In order to correctly implement the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency, to faithfully execute the policy of "education, persuasion, and redemption" and the principle of "education as the mainstay, punishment as the supplement" for minors who have committed illegal or criminal acts, to strive to achieve the working objectives of the reform of the juvenile justice trial system, to actively promote the standardized development of juvenile court work, and to vigorously advance the establishment and improvement of the socialist juvenile justice system with Chinese characteristics, the following opinions are hereby put forward for strengthening juvenile court work in the coming period.

I. Raise Ideological Awareness, Attach High Importance to Juvenile Court Work

1. Minors are the future and hope of the nation and the state. The Party and the state have always attached great importance to the protection of minors and have consistently regarded this work as an important component of the Party's and the state's undertakings. Safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of minors, preventing and correcting juvenile delinquency, and ensuring the healthy growth of minors are among the important responsibilities of the people's courts. Juvenile court work is an important platform for the people's courts to carry out judicial protection for minors and to actively participate in comprehensive social governance. Currently and for a period to come, juvenile court work can only be strengthened, not weakened.

2. Courts at all levels shall, from the perspective of practicing the guiding ideology of "Three Supremes," implementing the Scientific Outlook on Development, and building a harmonious society, fully recognize the importance and necessity of strengthening juvenile court work, faithfully implement the working policy of "upholding, perfecting, reforming, and developing," and place juvenile court work in an important position.

II. Strengthen Organizational Leadership, Establish and Improve Juvenile Court Institutions

3. Courts at all levels shall further strengthen the organizational leadership and professional guidance for juvenile court work, genuinely care for and support the institutional construction of juvenile courts, and create favorable conditions for the comprehensive and healthy development of juvenile court work.

4. The Supreme People's Court shall establish a "Juvenile Court Guidance Group" and set up a "Juvenile Court Work Office" within its Research Office, responsible for the daily guidance of juvenile courts nationwide.

5. High People's Courts shall establish a "Juvenile Court Guidance Group," with the head being a Vice President, and the group members shall include the heads of relevant trial divisions and administrative departments involved in cases concerning minors. The Juvenile Court Guidance Group of the High People's Court shall establish a "Juvenile Court Work Office" under it, responsible for the daily guidance of juvenile courts within its jurisdiction. The "Juvenile Court Work Office" shall be located within the Research Office or a trial division. High People's Courts may respectively establish collegiate benches for cases involving minors within their criminal trial divisions and civil trial divisions. If such collegiate benches have not yet been established, judges shall be designated to handle cases concerning minors on a full-time basis.

6. Intermediate People's Courts shall, based on the trial needs of cases concerning minors, gradually improve the construction of trial institutions for cases concerning minors. Intermediate People's Courts with the appropriate conditions may establish independent comprehensive trial divisions for cases concerning minors (hereinafter referred to as Juvenile Trial Divisions). For Intermediate People's Courts that have not yet established independent Juvenile Trial Divisions, collegiate benches for cases concerning minors shall be respectively established within their criminal trial divisions and civil trial divisions, or judges shall be designated to handle cases concerning minors on a full-time basis.

7. Basic People's Courts with the appropriate conditions may establish independent Juvenile Trial Divisions, or may, in accordance with the requirements of designated jurisdiction by Intermediate People's Courts, establish trial divisions that uniformly accept cases concerning minors. For Basic People's Courts that have not yet established independent Juvenile Trial Divisions or trial divisions that uniformly accept cases concerning minors, collegiate benches for cases concerning minors shall be respectively established within their criminal trial divisions and civil trial divisions, or judges shall be designated to handle cases concerning minors on a full-time basis.

8. The establishment and modification of Juvenile Court Guidance Groups, Juvenile Court Work Offices, and collegiate benches for cases concerning minors of High People's Courts shall be reported to the Juvenile Court Work Office of the Supreme People's Court. The establishment and modification of trial institutions for cases concerning minors of Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts shall be reported level by level to the Juvenile Court Work Office of the High People's Court.

III. Focus on Team Building, Enhance the Overall Quality of Juvenile Court Judges

9. Courts at all levels shall attach high importance to the team building of juvenile court judges, focusing on selecting judges with high political quality and strong professional competence, who are familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors, who are passionate about the protection of minors' rights and interests, and who are adept at conducting ideological education work for minors, to be responsible for hearing cases concerning minors.

10. Courts at all levels shall select people's assessors from among the staff of organizations such as the Communist Youth League, Women's Federations, trade unions, and schools to hear cases concerning minors. People's assessors hearing cases concerning minors shall be familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors, possess certain knowledge of juvenile pedagogy and psychology, and undergo necessary training.

11. Courts at all levels shall strengthen the training of juvenile court judges, continuously enhancing the overall quality of the juvenile court judge team. The Supreme People's Court and High People's Courts shall organize professional training for juvenile court judges at least once a year. Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts shall also regularly conduct professional training for juvenile court judges through various forms.

IV. Improve Work Systems, Strengthen the Functions and Roles of Juvenile Courts

12. Courts at all levels shall summarize and improve the characteristic work systems that have proven effective in trial practice, strengthen the functions and roles of juvenile courts, and enhance the effectiveness of the work.

13. When hearing criminal cases involving minors, people's courts with the appropriate conditions shall, for the investigation reports formed by relevant organizations or individuals that reflect the minor's personality characteristics, family situation, social interactions, growth experience, and behavior before and after committing the alleged crime, conduct in-court examination of evidence, carefully listen to the opinions of both the prosecution and defense on the investigation report, and give comprehensive consideration when imposing the sentence. When necessary, the people's court may also entrust relevant social organizations to conduct investigations on the above circumstances or conduct the investigation itself.

On the basis of summarizing experience in juvenile trial work and in light of actual circumstances, people's courts shall actively standardize and improve the social investigation report system, effectively resolve issues concerning the qualifications of social investigators, the content of investigation reports, and working procedures, and fully leverage the role of social investigation reports in trials.

14. People's courts shall generally try cases in which minors and adults jointly commit crimes in separate proceedings. For cases that should have been prosecuted separately but were not, the people's court may make recommendations to the prosecutorial authority.

15. People's courts may, taking into account the physical and mental characteristics of minors, adopt a roundtable trial format for cases involving minor defendants in minor offenses or negligent crimes, and for civil and administrative cases in which a minor is one of the parties.

16. When hearing criminal cases involving minors, people's courts shall focus on in-court education for the minor defendant. The main content of the in-court education includes: understanding of the relevant laws and regulations, analysis of the reasons the minor committed the alleged act, lessons to be drawn, the harm of the criminal act to society, the family, and the individual, whether criminal punishment should be imposed, how to correctly view the court's judgment, and issues to be noted when accepting community corrections or serving a sentence in a correctional facility. People's courts may invite persons conducive to the education, persuasion, and redemption of the minor offender to participate in the in-court education.

When hearing civil and administrative cases involving minors, people's courts shall pay attention to providing targeted education and guidance to the parties from the perspective of protecting the rights and interests of minors and resolving disputes.

17. For minor offenders whose criminal circumstances are minor, or who are first-time or occasional offenders, and who meet the conditions for the application of non-custodial penalties, non-custodial penalties shall be applied according to law. For minor offenders whose household registration is not local, the people's court shall strengthen contact with the community corrections department in its jurisdiction, or contact the local community corrections department through the people's court in the minor offender's place of household registration, to ensure the lawful application of non-custodial penalties.

18. For minor offenders whose judgments or rulings have already become legally effective, when transferring the legal documents for execution to the executing authority, the people's court shall simultaneously attach materials such as the social investigation report and the minor's behavior during the trial. For minor offenders who are serving sentences in juvenile correctional institutions or receiving community corrections, the people's court shall assist the juvenile correctional institution or the community corrections department in conducting assistance and education work.

People's courts shall conduct post-judgment follow-up visits for civil and administrative cases involving minors, striving to create a favorable environment for the healthy growth of minors.

People's courts shall record or prepare reports on the post-judgment tracking, assistance, education, and follow-up visits, and such records or reports shall be placed in the case files.

V. Deepen Reform and Exploration, Promote the Orderly Development of Juvenile Court Work

19. Courts at all levels shall actively engage in exchanges of theoretical achievements and practical experience in juvenile justice, further deepening the reform of juvenile justice.

20. Courts at all levels shall, based on the actual needs of safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of minors, preventing, correcting, and reducing juvenile delinquency, actively explore trial and enforcement methods suitable for the characteristics of cases involving minors, such as cross-regional social investigation, psychological evaluation and intervention, criminal case reconciliation, sentencing standardization, community corrections and judicial aid, and sealing of records for minor offenses.

21. Courts at all levels shall adhere to the principle of "special and priority" protection, boldly explore and practice characteristic trial systems for civil and administrative cases involving minors, such as social observation, roundtable trials, and litigation education guidance, and continuously develop new ideas and methods for the trial of civil and administrative cases involving minors.

VI. Actively Coordinate and Cooperate, Establish Supporting Mechanisms for Juvenile Court Work

22. Courts at all levels shall, under the leadership and coordination of the Party Committee Political and Legal Affairs Committee, strengthen communication with public security, procuratorial, judicial administrative, and other departments at the same level, actively establish and improve the "political and legal one-stop" working mechanism, and form a joint force for effectively preventing, correcting, and reducing juvenile delinquency.

23. Courts at all levels shall strengthen coordination and cooperation with relevant functional departments, social organizations, and groups, actively establish and improve the "social one-stop" working mechanism, strive to mobilize social forces, promote the implementation of resettlement and assistance and education measures for minor offenders, ensure that civil and administrative cases involving minors are properly handled, and promote the establishment and improvement of assistance systems for minors involved in litigation.

24. Courts at all levels shall strengthen legal education and publicity on the protection of minors, promote a social climate of respecting, protecting, and educating minors, educate and help minors to safeguard their own legitimate rights and interests, and enhance their awareness and ability for self-protection.

25. Courts at all levels shall, under the leadership and coordination of the Party Committee Political and Legal Affairs Committee, actively negotiate with relevant departments to promote the formulation of normative documents in their respective regions on issues such as social investigation of minors, judicial aid, and return to school and resettlement, and effectively resolve related issues.

VII. Improve Assessment and Guarantees, Consolidate the Foundation of Juvenile Court Work

26. Courts at all levels shall, based on the actual conditions of juvenile court work in their regions, include work such as extended assistance and education outside the courtroom and participation in comprehensive social governance as performance appraisal indicators within the scope of performance evaluation.

27. Courts at all levels shall, in light of the characteristics of trials of cases involving minors, increase investment in funding, equipment, and staffing for juvenile courts, and provide necessary guarantees for juvenile courts to carry out extended assistance and education outside the courtroom, legal education and publicity, and participation in comprehensive social governance.
